prepper_tips.title: Emergency Water: Boiling
prepper_tips.content: Bring water to a rolling boil for 1 minute (3 mins above 6,500ft) to kill most pathogens.

prepper_tips.title: Emergency Water: Bleach
prepper_tips.content: Add 8 drops of unscented household bleach per gallon of clear water; let stand for 30 minutes.

prepper_tips.title: Emergency Water: SODIS
prepper_tips.content: Fill clear PET bottles and leave in direct sunlight for 6 hours (2 days if cloudy) to disinfect via UV.

prepper_tips.title: Emergency Water: Pre-Filtering
prepper_tips.content: Always filter murky water through a clean cloth or coffee filter before disinfecting.

prepper_tips.title: Emergency Water: Distillation
prepper_tips.content: Boil water and collect the steam as it condenses to remove salts and some heavy metals.

prepper_tips.title: Medicinal Plants: Yarrow
prepper_tips.content: Identify by its feathery leaves. Use crushed leaves as a poultice to stop bleeding and disinfect wounds.

prepper_tips.title: Medicinal Plants: Willow Bark
prepper_tips.content: Contains salicin (aspirin precursor). Simmer bark in water for 15 mins to relieve pain and fever.

prepper_tips.title: Medicinal Plants: Plantain
prepper_tips.content: Found in lawns. Chew leaves and apply to stings, bites, or rashes for immediate relief.

prepper_tips.title: Medicinal Plants: Mullein
prepper_tips.content: Identify by fuzzy leaves. Steep leaves in hot water for a tea that relieves congestion and coughs.

prepper_tips.title: Medicinal Plants: Blackberry Leaf
prepper_tips.content: Astringent properties make it excellent as a tea for treating diarrhea and sore throats.

prepper_tips.title: Medicinal Plants: Calendula
prepper_tips.content: Antiseptic and skin healer. Use flower petals in salves or infusions for cuts and burns.

prepper_tips.title: Medicinal Plants: Dandelion Root
prepper_tips.content: A powerful bitter tonic. Simmer roots for a decoction that supports liver and digestive health.

prepper_tips.title: Medicinal Plants: Jewelweed
prepper_tips.content: Often grows near poison ivy. Crush the juicy stems and apply the sap to neutralize poison ivy oils.

prepper_tips.title: Medicinal Plants: Echinacea
prepper_tips.content: Coneflower root infusions can help boost the immune system at the onset of a cold.

prepper_tips.title: Medicinal Plants: Pine Needles
prepper_tips.content: Extremely high in Vitamin C. Steep fresh green needles in hot water for a nutritional survival tea.

prepper_tips.title: Fire Starting: Dryer Lint
prepper_tips.content: Dryer lint is an excellent free tinder. Store it in egg cartons for quick fire starters.

prepper_tips.title: Fire Starting: Bow Drill
prepper_tips.content: A primitive method using friction. Requires dry wood and practice to master.

prepper_tips.title: Food Storage: Mylar Bags
prepper_tips.content: Use with oxygen absorbers for long-term storage of dry goods like rice and beans.

prepper_tips.title: First Aid: Tourniquet
prepper_tips.content: Learn the proper placement to stop life-threatening limb bleeding.

prepper_tips.title: Navigation: Sun Compass
prepper_tips.content: Use a stick and its shadow to find East and West during the day.

prepper_tips.title: Shelter: Debris Hut
prepper_tips.content: A simple survival shelter made from fallen branches and leaves for insulation.

prepper_tips.title: Signal: Mirror
prepper_tips.content: A small mirror can reflect sunlight for miles to signal rescuers.

prepper_tips.title: Knot Tying: Bowline
prepper_tips.content: A critical knot that forms a fixed loop at the end of a rope.

prepper_tips.title: Wild Edibles: Pine Nuts
prepper_tips.content: Found in pine cones. High in protein and calories.

prepper_tips.title: Wild Edibles: Cattail
prepper_tips.content: The 'supermarket of the swamp.' Roots and young shoots are edible.

prepper_tips.title: Self Defense: Awareness
prepper_tips.content: The most important tool is situational awareness. Avoid conflict before it starts.

prepper_tips.title: Water Collection: Dew
prepper_tips.content: Tie clean rags around your ankles and walk through tall grass at dawn to collect dew.

prepper_tips.title: Tool Care: Sharpening
prepper_tips.content: Keep your knives and axes sharp; a dull tool is more dangerous than a sharp one.

prepper_tips.title: Clothing: Layering
prepper_tips.content: Base layer for moisture, mid-layer for warmth, outer layer for wind/rain.

prepper_tips.title: Mental Prep: Rule of Threes
prepper_tips.content: 3 mins without air, 3 hours without shelter, 3 days without water, 3 weeks without food.
